stemMd: The author mentions "a hand lens, a field guide and a patient afternoon" in order to

options.label: A
options.textMd: emphasise how simple and inexpensive the method of ranking sites was.

options.label: B
options.textMd: explain why the early surveys took several years to complete.

options.label: C
options.textMd: show that lichens can be identified only by trained specialists.

options.label: D
options.textMd: contrast the method with gas measurement, which the author says was faster.

options.label: E
options.textMd: suggest that lichen surveys were unreliable because amateurs carried them out.

explanationMd:
When a detail is offered as a list, ask what the list adds up to. Here it follows the claim that scientists "could rank the sites by air quality without a single gas measurement", and it is introduced by "using nothing more than". The items are ordinary: a magnifying lens, an identification book and one afternoon of careful looking. Together they show that the method needed little equipment, little money and little time.

The other choices give the list a purpose the text does not support: casting doubt on the method, restricting it to specialists, making it slow, or comparing its speed with gas measurement. The last paragraph confirms the reading: "The method is still cheap", where "still" implies it was cheap from the start.

distractorRationale.e: The passage says scientists used the method to rank sites and presents it as a working way to do so. The list stresses how simple the tools are, not any weakness of the surveyors.
distractorRationale.c: The list is of ordinary tools and time, introduced by "nothing more than", which points to a simple method. Nothing suggests that only specialists could use it.
distractorRationale.b: The list mentions a single afternoon, which points to a quick survey, not one lasting years.
distractorRationale.d: The passage makes no claim about how fast gas measurement is. It says only that the ranking needed no gas measurement at all.

accessibilityText: A purpose question about the lichen passage. It asks why the author mentions "a hand lens, a field guide and a patient afternoon". The five choices: to emphasise how simple and inexpensive the method of ranking sites was; to explain why the early surveys took several years; to show that lichens can be identified only by trained specialists; to contrast the method with gas measurement, which the author says was faster; to suggest lichen surveys were unreliable because amateurs carried them out.

provenance.notes: Original item written for this bank against an original passage. Every option is answerable, or refutable, from the passage text alone.

review.author: tolc-e-wave6-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: The phrase 'nothing more than' a hand lens, a field guide and a patient afternoon stresses how simple and cheap the method is, and the last paragraph confirms the method is cheap. B contradicts the single afternoon. C contradicts the simple equipment. D invents a speed comparison. E invents unreliability and amateurs. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave6-tolce-verbal-run2) reached the same answer: The phrase follows 'without a single gas measurement, using nothing more than', which stresses how simple and cheap the method was. B is wrong because an afternoon is not years. C and E are wrong because a field guide suggests non-specialists could do the work, and the passage never calls the surveys unreliable. D is wrong because the passage never says gas measurement was faster.]

review.notes: Uniqueness check: the list follows "without a single gas measurement" and the last paragraph says the method is "still cheap", so only the simplicity-and-cost reading is supported. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key.
